root.stage: The Badger turns from the rail. Behind him, the city keeps its lights on.
root.speech: Evening. You found the promenade, so you're either lost or curious. Both are fine. What do you want to know?

work.speech: I run two engineering teams at Derivco. Player accounts and player balances: the parts of the system that must never be wrong, at a hundred billion requests a month. My job is to keep the people sharp and the path clear.

options.label: What does a good week look like?

path.speech: Tester first, in Durban, 2015. Then developer, then tech lead, then two years consulting through Entelect for eBay, Adevinta, FNZ and MunichRe. Back to Derivco in Cape Town, and into management in 2025. Every step taught me a different way to break things.

options.label: What does a good week look like?

week.speech: A roadmap the team believes in. One hard conversation had early instead of late. A deploy nobody noticed. And a junior who ships something they were scared of last month.

games.speech: Before any of this I ran EGMR, a games site, for five years. Reviews, podcasts, press badges, deadlines. Games taught me that a system is only as good as the choice it puts in front of a person. That's still the whole job.

games_influences.speech: BioWare, mostly. Dragon Age for the idea that every companion has a reason. Mass Effect for the idea that a good interface is a promise you keep. Also far too many hours in spreadsheets pretending to be strategy games.

badger.stage: He shrugs, which on a badger is mostly ears.
badger.speech: Small, stubborn, unbothered by things larger than itself. Digs until the problem is out of the ground. I didn't pick it. It fit.

looking.speech: People who want to build things properly and are honest when they haven't. If that's you, the sheet has the details and the CV has the dates. LinkedIn is where I answer.
